tools.name: extract
tools.description: Fetch any public web page URL and get clean, LLM-ready text or Markdown: main content, code blocks, tables, links and headings, for RAG and agent context. Static HTML, Markdown or text; optional section ID. Default 20,000 output characters, max 100,000; input 2 MiB. No JavaScript rendering (see /extract/rendered), logins or paywalls. Empty pages, bad sections, browser challenges and errors are not charged. Use to read docs or articles. Example: url=https://example.com. Price $0.002/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 25 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to fetch

maxChars.description: Maximum characters of body text to return (500-100000, default 20000)

format.description: Returned representation: text (default), markdown, or both. HTML structured details are included in every format; Markdown/plain sources have empty details.

section.description: Optional exact visible HTML ID within primary content, 1-500 characters. Heading scope includes subsections until next same/higher-level heading; section/article/main/div scope is its subtree. Missing/ambiguous/unsupported targets fail uncharged. URL fragments alone do not select a section.

sourceMetadata.description: Page-level source declarations, not verified authorship or freshness. Head author/Open Graph date tags and bounded direct Schema.org JSON-LD Article/WebPage-like nodes only; exact-URL matches preferred, otherwise only one identity-free candidate. Author @id references resolve only to unambiguous local Person/Organization names, with both paths recorded. No external context/reference fetching or general JSON-LD expansion. Separate 2000-character value+provenance budget; 5 authors/10 dates. Original date strings are not normalized. Empty for Markdown/plain sources; unrelated entities and ambiguous nodes are omitted with warnings.

linkBaseUrl.description: Effective source-derived HTTP(S) base for links: the first supported HTML base href outside inert/foreign subtrees, otherwise finalUrl. Credentials and non-HTTP(S) base values are ignored with a warning. HTML links/canonical use this base; raw Markdown keeps relative syntax and can be resolved using this field. No linked resource is fetched. This static interpretation does not evaluate scripts or Content Security Policy.

sourceFormat.description: Source interpretation. Markdown is identified by text/markdown, or a .md/.markdown final path served as text/plain (warned). Markdown syntax is retained verbatim within the cap, not converted to HTML or parsed for structured details; text also retains that syntax. HTML section IDs are unsupported for Markdown/plain text.

textLength.description: Full extracted text length before the character cap, within the input limit.

truncated.description: Input or requested primary representation is incomplete. Structured detail limits are reported separately in warnings.

id.description: Source HTML heading ID or direct child anchor ID, when present and supported; not a generated slug.

section.description: Null for full primary-content reading. Otherwise the explicitly requested scope; title/description/canonical remain page-level metadata. Heading scope ends before the next same/higher-level heading, including nested subsections; container scope is its subtree.
